opportunities.title: Commercial Kitchen Exhaust (Hood) Cleaning Service
opportunities.idea: Deep-clean grease from commercial kitchen exhaust hoods, ducts and fans for restaurants, hotels, cafeterias, cloud kitchens. Compliance-mandated recurring service.

why_passes: Mandatory + recurring demand: fire-safety code means every commercial kitchen MUST have exhaust cleaned on a fixed schedule (quarterly for high-volume). Customer has no way out and cannot DIY — strongest possible cash-flow signal.
Net margins 25-40% per job; a single-truck operation with certified techs can do ~USD 600k/yr revenue; two trucks = seven figures.
Low capex ~Rs 5-15 L — fits 1 Cr entry with huge headroom. 40-60 accounts within a 15-mile radius is the profitable route-density target.
India providers already proven: Mumbai (OXY, Accordible), Bangalore (deepcleaning.in, EPSCO) — market is real, not theoretical.
unit_economics: Per-job pricing: Rs 3,000-15,000+ for a single hood; mid-size restaurants Rs 8,000-15,000; large hotels Rs 15,000-30,000. Global comps: USD 450-650/system, emergency cleans USD 800+.
Recurring contracts (MSAs) lock in recurring revenue: a 10-hood quarterly account ~USD 2,200/visit at ~55% margin before overhead.
A real 60-day practitioner case study built 30 accounts / USD 60k/yr; a hospital-network example scaled to USD 850k/yr by year 2.
watchouts: Labour + night work is the core constraint: dirty, after-hours (11pm-4am), heavy PPE. Hard to hire reliable night staff.

CERTIFICATION GAP: 67% of these businesses fail between months 12-24, often from underpricing by 40-60%, scattered routes, and buying worthless online certifications that fire marshals/insurers don't recognise. Use approved in-person cert bodies.
India fire-code enforcement is less uniformly strict than the US — the 'mandatory' moat is weaker for small independents; pitch the compliance/insurance angle to larger chains where it bites.
Insurance: general liability does NOT cover grease-fire claims that happen after you leave. Get specialised cover vetted by a commercial-liability attorney.

opportunities.title: Water Tanker / Bulk Water Supply (housing societies, construction, commercial)
opportunities.idea: Own/operate a small fleet of water tankers supplying bulk water to housing societies, construction sites, and industrial/commercial buildings.
opportunities.verdict: WEAK-MEDIUM (do not pursue as fresh entry)

why_rejected: Demand is real but the moat is ERODING on live 2026 data: BWSSB's Sanchari Cauvery scheme (launched May 2025) delivered 30,000+ tankers / Rs 5+ crore by April 2026 and has already cut private tanker demand ~60% in some pockets.
Heavy regulation: Karnataka fixed 12,000L at Rs 1,200; forced registration with BBMP; GPS tracking mandates; 200+ private tankers taken over by the state.
Documented union/mafia behavior (blocking competitors, coercion, E.coli water scandals) makes fresh entry structurally contested and reputationally dangerous.
Government is effectively the competitor: BWSSB is adding municipal supply (Cauvery V Stage augmenting to 400-450 MLD; 3 lakh connections targeted by 2028).
unit_economics: Even at regulated caps: Rs 700-1,500 per 6,000-12,000L trip; peak-crisis prices reached Rs 2,200-2,500/12,000L in Bengaluru 2024-25.
Pune market benchmark: ~Rs 23 cr/day, 3,500 tankers, 22,000-30,000 trips/day, 20% of population dependent.
BUT margins are being squeezed by municipal supply expansion — the long-run thesis is negative for private entrants.
watchouts: This is the canonical 'pattern-based intuition looks good, live data says otherwise' example — exactly why the hunter pulls fresh 2026/27 sources instead of stale training logic.
Kept in the database as a documented negative case to show the reasoning, not as a recommendation.
